item.title: Juneau Assembly stalls on whether to disempower Eaglecrest Ski Area’s board
item.description: Earlier this month, Mayor Beth Weldon proposed an ordinance to reduce the status of the city-owned ski area’s board from an empowered board to an advisory board.

item.title: Skagway students are asking for time off school to participate in subsistence activities
item.description: The student council is calling on the Skagway School Board to make the attendance policy more inclusive by allowing students to take seven subsistence days per semester.

item.title: Union contract negotiations spark student outrage in support of Juneau teachers
item.description: Students are speaking out about how unresolved contract negotiations between the district and its teaching and support staff unions are affecting them in the classroom.

item.title: Republican Sens. Murkowski and Tillis call for Noem to resign
item.description: Murkowski says the Homeland Security secretary should be held to account for her agency's tactics in Minneapolis, where two citizens have been shot to death amid a massive immigration enforcement operation.

item.title: Scientists confirm climate change is making destructive landslides more frequent across Alaska — especially in Southeast
item.description: Climate change is making atmospheric rivers more extreme and researchers have traced a 295% increase in landslides reported in the news between the 1980s and 2010s.

item.title: Juneau’s new avalanche advisor started right before recent evacuations
item.description: John Bressette joined the city just before record snowfall, followed by rain and flooding, pushed the community to declare a disaster and issue evacuation advisories downtown.

item.title: Haines animal cruelty case at a standstill as defendant says he’s in Russia and plans to stay there
item.description: There will be no trial as long as Steve Kroschel remains overseas, the judge said at a hearing last week.

item.title: Tustumena replacement project out to bid, new ferry to sail in 2029
item.description: The state's project notice calls for the new mainliner ferry to be completed by the beginning of 2029 with an estimated price tag of more than $300 million.
